short: The Roanoke Colony was England's first attempt to establish a permanent settlement in the Americas, ending in its mysterious disappearance.
full:
Sponsored by Sir Walter Raleigh, the first English settlement attempt on Roanoke Island was established in 1585, but was abandoned a year later due to food shortages and conflict with the local Algonquian population. A second group of 117 settlers, including women and children, arrived in July 1587 under the governorship of John White.

White returned to England for supplies later that year, but his voyage back was delayed by the outbreak of the Anglo-Spanish War. When he finally returned on 18 August 1590, the settlement was completely deserted, with only the word "CROATOAN" carved into a palisade post. The "Lost Colony" provided brutal lessons about the logistical and diplomatic challenges of transatlantic settlement that informed later, successful ventures.
